items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: Yes, that's right. Yes, we did have Claude.

ctx.x: Basie, no Freddie Greene? Oh no, you had Claude Williams?
Yes, that's right. Yes, we did have Claude. But see, he didn't really play the in/Reno with us, but he did make, he did go with us to New York.

items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: And Buck Clayton just happened to come through because Buck lived in Parsons, Kansas and he’d been living out here in L.A. So that’s what happened with me joining Count.

ctx.x: Yeah well we’re jumping a long ways. Different times we’d have down in Florida — you know that was down south and quite segregated then, you know. And we played some dances for whites that the colored couldn’t go to, and then we played some for colored that they wouldn’t let the whites go to down south. They were all messed up like that. Like I say I heard Joe Venuti. I was standing almost about a block, at least a half a block from the pavilion, about as close as I could get to him, and he was in my home town in…

called Hot Lips Page, he was there. See he had two different bands I think to pick from because the Blue Devils had broke up and there was some of them which — Hot Lips and Walter Page was the Blue Devils and Lester came up there with the Blue Devils, and so he really didn’t have too much more after he got me to finish out the rhythm section. And Buck Clayton just happened to come through because Buck lived in Parsons, Kansas and he’d been living out here in L.A. So that’s what happened with me joining Count.
When did you do your first recordings?
